rationale: C11 plausibly supplied a material rhetorical and functional template for the later appeal. Both texts address an urgent industrial labor dispute by stressing continued bargaining, a settlement fair to both sides, wage-and-price stability, and the national harm of a shutdown. C02 is also structurally close in urging that the parties be allowed to reach a settlement in the national interest, while C18 shares the distinctive appeal to labor-management “statesmanship,” but neither combines as many of the child's elements as C11.

shared_material.child_excerpt: achieve a settlement which is fair and reasonable to both shareholders and workers and which preserves price stability in the industry
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Neither the union nor the steel companies could expect to be satisfied with the recommendations which would, all things considered, be fair to both parties.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the desired labor settlement as an equitable accommodation between management and labor.

shared_material.child_excerpt: which preserves price stability in the industry
shared_material.parent_excerpt: if we are going to establish fair price ceilings... And if we let prices--and wages--go up... we would obviously not be preventing inflation
shared_material.explanation: Both connect resolution of the labor dispute with restraint of prices and wages.

shared_material.child_excerpt: make an all out effort to achieve a just settlement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the parties resumed negotiations and Government negotiators on the scene were hopeful of settlement
shared_material.explanation: Both emphasize last-stage negotiations as the means to secure settlement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Our country at this juncture in our affairs can ill afford a shutdown in this important segment of our economy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Taft-Hartley Act simply would not have prevented a shutdown of essential steel production in this case... without irreparable harm to the national interest.
shared_material.explanation: Both justify presidential intervention by portraying an industrial shutdown as an unacceptable threat to the national interest.
